content.comment_body: I use a [product_name] with additional I/O modules for managing my home's heating system. I purchased it as part of a starter kit, which included [product_name] software. The provided DVD has [product_name] [version_no], and I am wondering if this version is compatible with Ubuntu 20.04.1 LTS. I'm considering installing it on a low-power computer (AMD C-60 CPU, 11W) since the current Windows 7 installation seems unstable. I prefer not to upgrade the computer, as the entire heating system operates behind a UPS.
Hello, Have you checked this thread: [url] Best regards, [user_name]
Yes, I've seen it and downloaded the provided text file. My main concern is whether my [version_no] is too outdated, and if it will actually work on much newer Linux distributions.

Hello, You can consider upgrading to the latest [product_name]; see this link: [url] Also, this link may assist with installing a downloaded upgrade for [product_name]: [url] Best regards, [user_name]

Thanks for sharing those links. I encountered an export restriction firewall and will wait a week for a confirmation email. Update: I received the confirmation email. Although it took some time, I now have the software required.

analysis.insight_summary: The user needed advice on running an older version of [product_name] on a current Linux distribution due to hardware limitations and reliability issues with their Windows 7 system. Key user experience challenges included compatibility uncertainty and a delay caused by export restrictions while acquiring the software. The process to obtain the necessary software was not entirely straightforward, primarily due to waiting for confirmation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects their current [product_name] to function reliably on a newer Linux operating system, or that there will be a clear upgrade path. They also hope for minimal disruption to the heating control system during any transition.
